This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #33113: Sessions assigned `project_id = 'global'` across multiple directories, causing /sessions to list all sessions globally with no project scoping
- #39667: Two directories sharing a project ID cause session tabs to show the wrong project's name in the Web UI (explicitly identifies the `global` ID fallback as the root cause)
- #35873: Two projects sharing the same git remote URL collide into one project ID — same underlying project resolution mechanism
- #39676: Different folders treated as the same project when they share git identity

These issues all stem from the same root cause in `Project.resolve`: directories without a distinguishing git remote or root commit fall back to `id = "global"`, causing session leakage across unrelated directories.

This issue might be a duplicate of or related to existing issues. Please check:
- #33332: Configurable worktree creation — base ref, branch naming, repo-relative path — this feature request covers the same underlying problem (worktree always branching from HEAD with no way to select a base ref) and proposes a design to address it, including a clickable branch UI and `baseRef` config option.

- #36731: Same root cause — `worktree.ready` listener only lives in the legacy layout, causing the first prompt to stall forever in the new layout.

I reviewed the potential duplicates mentioned by the bot.

**#35090 (server-side network resilience)** — That issue is about making the Desktop/Server architecture survive restricted networks. This issue is about client-side UX: the shell tool hanging for 60-120s before failing. Different layer, different fix.

**#30611 (automatic retry on transient errors)** — That issue proposes retrying automatically when network errors occur. This one proposes the opposite: fast failure when the network is clearly unreachable. The two are complementary — do a quick pre-flight check first (e.g. \curl --connect-timeout 3\); if the probe fails, fast-fail immediately; if the probe succeeds but the actual request fails, then retry. But right now there is no probe, just a blind 60-120s wait.

I don't think either is a true duplicate.

AI SDK support is intentionally deferred from this PR. An initial implementation used `AsyncLocalStorage` to bridge per-session callbacks into cached AI SDK providers, but we removed it to keep this hook explicit and native-only.
